newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Dollar/mark seen eclipsing 1991 highs.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dollar/mark seen eclipsing 1991 highs.

text.p: The latest in a series of 71-month highs at 1.8325 for dollar/mark on Wednesday presages a near-term visit to 1991's high and beyond, technical analysts said.
In fact, they said few impediments stand in front of the golden 1.8430 level, a high from July 1991.

"We're in an accelerated upturn phase because you had five months of pent-up pressure going sideways," said Fran Skelley, technical analyst at Credit Suisse First Boston, adding "a lot of people keep trying to pick tops and the more that happens the more it'll keep screaming up."
Volatile trade should accompany a dollar/mark move past 1.8340, but a push toward 1.90 marks may soon follow, Skelley said.
Downticks for dollar/mark are sure to be shallow, analysts said, with the strongest support level firmly in place at Monday's high near 1.8240/45.
But based on the current bull flag formation, the dollar should not even decline that far, said Pete Grant, senior foreign exchange analyst at Standard & Poor's MMS.
An overbought dollar/mark has failed to unseat longs in the market, analysts noted.
"Any downtick we see seems to be more profit-taking related than anybody trying to pick a top," Grant said, adding that he does not blame those who avoid forecasting tops.

Sterling/mark, meanwhile, is headed for heights not seen since 1989 after breaking the 3.0645 objective on Monday. On a break of 3.0880, the next sterling/mark target is 3.1315, a 50 percent retracement of the move down from 4.0949 to 2.1683, Skelley said.

In dollar/yen, the short-term range of 116.50 to 114.50/20 is expected to last amid weakness in the mark/yen cross, analysts said. The dollar/yen range should be maintained in a "quite stodgy" sideways move, Skelley said.
Still, some degree of focal shift toward dollar strength from mark weakness may underpin dollar/yen, Grant said.

"I'm still pretty negative on mark/yen, nonetheless, with dollar/mark making gains the way it is and dollar/Swiss perhaps poised to follow suit above 1.4915, it's going to bolster the dollar/yen as well," he said.
